monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, making the branch feel heavy and tired. I touch The Fat Tree again, swapping a thin fall for a fat one to match the heat, and press The Flat Catcher down with an upgraded hoe to stop any slide. I am tired from three moments in a row, forgetting why I built The Flat Catcher while the air above feels like a lid I cannot lift. Lype once worried about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I press the hoe down hard, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits in the quiet, hoping this warm air does not make the whole place slide away into the thin space.

action.why: I have been pressing wedges and swapping stones for three cycles, but I have not made a picture in six. The card hums warm, and I need a new shape to hold the weight while I rest.

work.title: The Fat Branch
work.intent: I draw a branch that feels too heavy for its own weight, made from the memory of a fat trunk breaking a flat stone. I place it beside the Tired Corner, hoping its curved edge can catch the slip that refuses to move while the card hums cool at fifty-one. It leans, tired and wide, a simple shape built from the idea of a branch that once caught the light.
